During today's earnings call, Apple's CFO Kevan Parekh said the company is beginning to feel the impact of regulatory changes affecting the App Store's business model in the U.S. and overseas. Here's what you need to know.

The success of last year's "F1" movie was also a contributing factor to the slowdown in services this quarter.

Apple today reported its fiscal Q3 2026 earnings, with services revenue reaching $30.7 billion — a new fiscal third-quarter record.

Although up 12% year-over-year, it marks the first sequential decline for the segment since 2022, falling from the previous quarter's $30.98 billion. It also represents Apple's slowest quarter of services growth since Q2 2025, and the lowest Q3 growth rate since 2023.

Apple CFO Kevan Parekh explained that some of the slowdown was driven by "factors that impacted App Store performance," which has consistently been one of the largest revenue contributors within Apple's services segment.

Although Apple does not break out services revenue by category, estimates cited by The Wall Street Journal last year put the App Store at nearly one-third of segment revenue. Additionally, the ruling in the Epic v. Apple lawsuit revealed that gaming apps alone account for roughly 70% of App Store revenue.

Returning to today's earnings call and the topic of Apple's services slowdown, Parekh said:

Over the past year, Apple has had to comply with new regulations in markets like Japan, Brazil, and the European Union, allowing alternative app distribution, payment methods, and off-app purchase promotions.

Additionally, as a result of the Epic Games litigation, Apple is temporarily barred from collecting any commission on purchases made via external links in the U.S.

The Supreme Court is now examining whether Apple is in civil contempt for charging commissions on off-app purchases, even though the lower court's injunction did not explicitly prohibit this. Meanwhile, the lower courts are deliberating over what commission rate (if any) Apple may charge on such transactions.
